source.title: Generalization emerges from local optimization in a self-organized learning network

record.tranche_reason: The study tests for a grokking-like generalization transition using a different learning method and measure: an evolving lookup-table network and generalization error versus the amount of training data.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own generalization results for the proposed network. It does not measure the original gradient-trained models or optimization steps. Results cited from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study calls its result grokking but measures something else. It reports a sharp drop in generalization error as the fraction of learned examples r grows, in a non-gradient lookup-table network. Training error is zero by construction at every step. There is no optimization-time axis, so no delay of generalization after training saturates can occur or be measured. The result is a sample-size learning-curve threshold, a related but different construct from V1's delayed jump. None of V2–V7 is examined. Findings go to fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that their locally optimized, topology-evolving lookup-table network generalizes perfectly on several binary classification tasks, with an abrupt transition that resembles a first-order phase transition and that they call grokking. They also argue that learning and generalization become decoupled. They stress that this is a proof of concept limited to Ne≤12.
record.recipe_differences: The network stores examples in lookup tables and changes topology through local splitting, merging, and pruning; it has no global loss minimization or continuously adjusted weights.
record.method_sensitivity: The parity grokking threshold varies across training-set trajectories and across tasks. The reported threshold decreases and the transition sharpens as Ne increases.

fits_no_version.finding: A non-gradient, locally optimized lookup-table network reaches zero generalization error abruptly once the learned fraction r passes a threshold rg. For parity at Ne=10 this is about 0.13. rg is narrowly distributed across training sets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abrupt sample-size thresholds to perfect generalization on algorithmic tasks occur without gradient training or a global loss.

fits_no_version.finding: For parity, rg decreases and the transition sharpens as input size Ne increases from 5 to 12. The authors say the observations are identical for other tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The data-fraction generalization threshold shrinks and sharpens with input dimension.

fits_no_version.finding: The network generalizes on all six rule-based tasks, at task-dependent thresholds, and does not generalize on random labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The threshold for rule-based generalization is task-dependent, and random labels give no transition.

record.problems: The study is a proof of concept limited to Ne≤12. The authors report computational constraints, use 20 training sets for most curves, and state that error bars could be estimated correctly only for Ne=10. Detailed values for several task curves are presented only in figures. Training accuracy is zero by construction, and the study does not measure optimization steps or test accuracy beginning at chance.

untested.parts: There is no training-time trajectory, no train-accuracy saturation preceding the test jump (training error is always zero), and no delay that varies with training-set size.
Not examined: Fourier circuits, removal of memorizing components, or progress measures.
Not examined: non-algorithmic data, initialization scale, or weight norm.
Not examined: LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Not examined: weight decay or low-norm bias, critical dataset size under regularization, or ungrokking.
Not examined: whether runs converge to the same algorithm.
Not examined: optimizer or floating-point artifacts. The method has no gradient optimizer.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 'supports' label is removed. The study's 'grokking' is a threshold in training-set fraction, with training error identically zero, so it cannot show generalization delayed after training saturates. The rows stay as records of a related construct. Power et al. is cited only for context.

versions.untested_parts: It does not test a gradient-trained network's test-accuracy trajectory over optimization steps, whether accuracy begins at chance, or whether a smaller training set requires more optimization steps. Its training error is zero by construction, and it plots generalization error against the fraction of input cases learned.
It does not measure Fourier circuits, memorizing components being removed, or continuous progress measures anticipating a jump.
It does not test image, text, or molecule data, or vary initialization scale or weight norm.
It does not study LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
It does not test weight decay, low-norm bias, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
It does not compare identifiable algorithms learned across runs, architectures, or hyperparameters.
It does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits in softmax.

rows.subject: proposed self-organized learning network
rows.operation_detail: Sequentially learn training samples and remodel topology; measure generalization error as the training-set fraction changes.
rows.measure: Generalization error Eg versus relative training-set size r
rows.value: Eg eventually cancels out for r greater than ≃ 0.13
rows.note: The authors describe the generalization-error trajectory as fluctuating and its convergence as non-uniform. Training error is zero by construction.
rows.check: Eg reaches zero above r≃0.13 for one training set. This is a threshold in data fraction, not a delay in training time after train accuracy saturates, so it cannot show V1's effect.

rows.subject: proposed self-organized learning network
rows.operation_detail: Repeat parity learning with independent training sets and plot generalization error against r.
rows.measure: Generalization error Eg versus relative training-set size r
rows.value: Eg cancels out for a sufficiently large r>rg for every trajectory; the threshold rg depends on the trajectory
rows.note: The plotted blue curve is the mean generalization error over the 20 training sets; the text does not give a numerical mean threshold.
rows.check: Same construct as R1 across 20 training sets: a data-fraction threshold rg, with no training-time trajectory.

rows.subject: proposed self-organized learning network
rows.operation_detail: Estimate the probability distribution of the parity grokking threshold rg across independent training sets.
rows.value: Figure only; the text describes the probability distribution as narrow
rows.note: The distribution is a threshold measurement, not a measurement of optimization steps.
rows.check: This is the PDF of the data-size threshold rg over 220 sets (figure only). It is not a measure of delayed generalization.

rows.subject: proposed self-organized learning network
rows.operation_detail: Vary the number of input interface nodes and average parity generalization-error curves over training sets.
rows.measure: Generalization error Eg versus r; fitted threshold rg and transition-width parameter λ
rows.value: The authors report that rg decreases and the transition becomes sharper as Ne increases; individual curve values are figure only
rows.uncertainty: Relative error reported only for Ne=10: 3% for rg and 16% for λ
rows.note: This varies input size and reports thresholds in relative training-set size, not optimization time. The authors say asymptotic behavior at large Ne is inaccessible with their computational resources.
rows.check: rg decreases and the transition sharpens with input size Ne (5–12). This is input-size scaling of a sample threshold, not V1's delay-versus-training-set-size relation.

reader_labels.condition: Parity learning and the rule-based classification tasks tested by the proposed network
reader_labels.reason: The authors report a transition to zero generalization error after additional samples are learned (R1–R2), and report generalization on all tested tasks with a rule (R5–R11).
